My favourite transcription tool on the Mac, MacWhisper, is getting a major update today with new live meeting transcription, significantly improved speech recognition, deeper Apple Intelligence integration, and a brand-new transcription model. Here's what's new.

MacWhisper gets even deeper Apple Intelligence integration

I wrote in the past about how much I rely on MacWhisper, especially in my podcast workflow.

MacWhisper is one of the earliest AI transcription tools built for the Mac. Since independent developer Jordi Bruin released it in 2023, it has steadily evolved, expanding support for new models, services, and workflows.

That includes automatic meeting recording and transcription, folder watching, system-wide dictation, local and cloud AI models, and integrations with services like Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

Today, MacWhisper is being updated to version 15.2, introducing improved speech recognition powered by NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Diarization model, which was only unveiled a few hours ago.

Which brings me to the other major feature in today's update: live meeting transcription.

This feature has been near the top of MacWhisper's public development roadmap for some time, and now it's finally here, letting users review, reference, copy, or send live transcripts while a meeting is still in progress.

On the actual transcription model front, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model, supporting 22 languages, along with deeper integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts on macOS 27.

Users running macOS now, including in the EU, can search transcripts system-wide, open them with Siri, extract their text into Shortcuts, and reference the transcript on the current screen in Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 adds folders and subfolders for organising transcript files and meetings, with drag-and-drop support from the sidebar to move existing transcript files into them.
